method.scope: The accessible NYC Artist Coalition shared-folder population at capture time
method.rootSelection: All 61 root items were selected and reconciled before recursive folder capture.
method.recursion: Every accessible folder discovered through the interface was opened, inventoried, classified, and assigned one primary disposition.
method.contentReview: A priority set of 63 text documents was exported privately and close-read across the main civic, campaign, meeting, and implementation clusters.
method.privateCustody: Exact Drive identifiers, paths, filenames, owners, raw exports, excerpts, participant data, and the recursive manifest remain outside the public repository.

semanticClusters: Cabaret Law repeal and Let NYC Dance
Office of Nightlife and public town-hall production
M.A.R.C.H. accountability and Talks Not Raids
Commercial Rent Stabilization and Fair Rent NYC
priorityReview.boundary: Content review supports proposition-level summaries and research leads. It does not make the underlying documents public, clear collaborator quotations, or establish authorship where an artifact does not say who made it.

promotedFindings.summary: A protected working guide identifies Jamie and Julia Fredenburg as its writers and describes a repeatable method connecting community listening, priority-setting, coalition building, Council outreach, public events, campaign materials, and sustained follow-through.
promotedFindings.boundary: Treat the guide as shared authorship and operating-method evidence, not proof that either writer solely created every tactic or caused the legislative outcomes.

promotedFindings.summary: A protected run-of-show documents Jamie and Olympia Kazi opening the Office of Nightlife town hall for NYC Artist Coalition and assigns Jamie presentation and documentation tasks; contemporary public reporting independently identifies Jamie as a coalition speaker and the coalition as the town-hall convener.
promotedFindings.boundary: Do not convert a shared run-of-show into sole production credit or infer attendance, endorsement, or policy causation.

promotedFindings.summary: A protected implementation checklist headed for Jamie records completed Fair Rent NYC web tasks involving responsive presentation, testimonials, coalition and press modules, social sharing, data fixes, and campaign calls to action.
promotedFindings.boundary: Use this as corroboration of Jamie's implementation work, not sole authorship of campaign policy, copy, data, photography, design, or outcomes.

promotedFindings.summary: Meeting artifacts show a recurring practice of agendas, ballots, priority voting, next-step assignment, practical safety work, and translation from participant concerns into campaign and government-facing action.
promotedFindings.boundary: The records support the form of the practice, not participant consensus, universal experience, audited attendance, or Jamie's authorship of every artifact.

limitations: The census covers the population accessible to the authenticated account on July 19, 2026; deleted, removed, inaccessible, or never-shared material may exist outside it.
A folder or file's presence, owner label, or custody does not establish Jamie's authorship, approval, role, or permission to publish.
The whole population was inventoried and dispositioned; 63 priority documents were close-read. Content-reviewed total is intentionally smaller than population total.
Private working documents require public corroboration or collaborator review before stronger outcome, authorship, quotation, or causal claims are promoted.
Passing automated coverage and leakage checks does not complete Jamie review, collaborator review, rights review, application selection, or production approval.
